reason: E2 directly demonstrates that a TiNbZr-Ag alloy forms an amorphous-crystalline oxide nanocomposite surface via reactive wear protection, reducing wear by an order of magnitude, which supports the core mechanism and wear reduction premise. However, E2 does not report friction coefficient data or temperature-dependent performance, and E1 concerns a different 2D HEA nanoflake lubricant system unrelated to bulk Ag-alloyed HEAs, providing no support for the friction reduction, wide temperature range, or specific quantitative predictions.
premises: Adding Ag to an HEA promotes in-situ formation of a lubricious oxide nanocomposite tribolayer during sliding
The Ag-containing tribolayer reduces friction and wear via low-shear and self-healing mechanisms
This effect is effective across a wide temperature range (RT to ~600 °C)
The mechanism is 'reactive wear protection' where Ag facilitates oxidation and segregation at the contact interface
The predicted improvement is a 30–70% reduction in COF and up to two orders of magnitude decrease in wear rate
